lessons.title: Body Parts and Their Functions
lessons.notes_html:
Our Body Parts

Our body is made of many parts, and every part does a special job. The eye is used for seeing. With our eyes we see the things around us, their colours and their shapes.

Functions of the Main Parts

  • Teeth bite, chew, crush and grind the food we eat, so it breaks into small pieces.
  • The nose is used for breathing and for smelling. Through the nose, air reaches the lungs.
  • Muscles move the bones. When muscles contract and relax, the bones move and we can walk, run and lift things.
  • The skeleton is the framework of all the bones. It gives shape and support to the body and protects delicate parts like the brain, heart and lungs.
  • The heart pumps blood to all parts of the body, so food substances and oxygen reach every part.
  • The lungs are the main organs of breathing. They take oxygen from the air into the blood and remove the waste gas.
  • The stomach stores food and digests it. Its juices make the food soft and break it into small substances.

Key Points

  • The skeleton gives shape and support to the body.
  • The heart pumps blood to all parts of the body.
  • The lungs are our breathing organs.
  • Teeth bite, chew, crush and grind food.

mcqs.q: Which part of the body do we use for seeing?
mcqs.why: The eye is used for seeing. With the help of our eyes we can see the things around us, their colours and their shapes.

mcqs.q: What is the work of the teeth?
options: To bite, chew, crush and grind food
To give shape to the body
mcqs.why: Teeth bite, chew, crush and grind the food we eat, so the food breaks into small pieces and is digested easily in the stomach.

mcqs.q: The nose is used for breathing and for:
mcqs.why: The nose is used for breathing and for smelling. Through the nose air reaches the lungs, and we can recognise different smells.

mcqs.q: Which part pumps blood to all parts of the body?
mcqs.why: The heart pumps blood to all parts of the body. In this way food substances and oxygen reach every part of the body.

mcqs.q: The skeleton is the framework of all the:
mcqs.why: The skeleton is the framework of all the bones. It gives shape and support to the body and protects the delicate internal parts.

mcqs.q: Which organs are the main organs of breathing?
mcqs.why: The lungs are the main organs of breathing. They take oxygen from the air into the blood and remove the waste gas from the body.

mcqs.q: How do muscles help the body to move?
options: They pump blood to the bones
They move the bones when they contract and relax
mcqs.why: Muscles move the bones. When muscles contract and relax, the bones move, and so we can walk, run and lift things.

mcqs.q: What does the stomach do with the food?
options: It stores food and digests it
It pumps it to the lungs
It throws it out at once
mcqs.why: The stomach stores food and digests it. The juices of the stomach make the food soft and break it into small substances.

mcqs.q: Which part protects delicate internal parts such as the brain, heart and lungs?
mcqs.why: The skeleton gives shape and support to the body and also protects the delicate internal parts such as the brain, the heart and the lungs.

mcqs.q: The unscrambled word OETNSKEL is:
mcqs.why: The jumbled letters OETNSKEL make the word SKELETON, the framework of all the bones which gives shape and support to the body.

lessons.title: Digestion and the Digestive System
lessons.notes_html:
Where Digestion Begins

Digestion begins in the mouth. The teeth break the food into small pieces, and then the food travels through the body parts that digest food.

The Path of Food

  • First the food is chewed in the mouth.
  • Then it passes through the food pipe.
  • It reaches the stomach, which stores it and digests it with its juices.
  • Then it goes into the small intestine.
  • At last it passes into the large intestine.

A Model of the Digestive System

We can make a model of the digestive system with chart paper, a box, rubber tubing, polythene bags, a small plastic bottle, a used light bulb and a string. The tubing is used as the food pipe, the bottle or bag as the stomach, and a long tubing as the intestines.

Key Points

  • Digestion begins in the mouth.
  • Path of food: mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine, large intestine.
  • The stomach's juices make the food soft.

mcqs.q: Digestion begins in which part of the body?
mcqs.why: Digestion begins in the mouth, where the teeth bite, chew, crush and grind the food into small pieces.

mcqs.q: After the mouth, the food passes through the:
mcqs.why: The path of food is: mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine and large intestine. After the mouth comes the food pipe.

mcqs.q: Which part comes just after the stomach in the path of food?
mcqs.why: In the digestive system the food goes from the stomach into the small intestine, and at last into the large intestine.

mcqs.q: In a model of the digestive system, the rubber tubing is used as the:
mcqs.why: In the model, the tubing is used as the food pipe, the bottle or bag as the stomach and a long tubing as the intestines.

mcqs.q: The juices of the stomach do what to the food?
options: Make it soft and break it into small substances
Push it back to the mouth
mcqs.why: The juices of the stomach make the food soft and break it into small substances so that the body can use it.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the correct order of the path of food?
options: Mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
Mouth, large intestine, stomach, food pipe
mcqs.why: The correct path is mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine and then large intestine, as shown in the digestive system diagram.

mcqs.q: The last part in the path of food is the:
mcqs.why: After the small intestine, the food passes into the large intestine, which is the last part in the path of food.

mcqs.q: Why do the teeth break food into small pieces?
options: So it is digested easily in the stomach
mcqs.why: Teeth bite, chew, crush and grind food into small pieces, and in this way the food is digested easily in the stomach.

mcqs.q: In the model activity, the model is placed inside a:
mcqs.why: The parts are joined in order and the model is placed inside a large box to demonstrate how food is digested.

mcqs.q: Which material is used as the stomach in the model?
mcqs.why: The bottle or polythene bag is used as the stomach in the model, while the tubing works as the food pipe and intestines.

lessons.title: Keeping Our Body Healthy
lessons.notes_html:
Disorders and Their Prevention

  • Teeth: cavities and toothache. Brush the teeth twice a day and eat fewer sweet things.
  • Stomach: indigestion and stomach ache. Eat clean and fresh food on time.
  • Heart: fast heartbeat and heart diseases. Exercise daily and eat less oily food.
  • Lungs: cough and difficulty in breathing. Breathe in clean air and stay away from tobacco smoke.

Protecting Our Bones

Athletes should warm up before playing, wear protective things such as knee pads and elbow pads, and follow the rules of the game. Motor cyclists should always wear a helmet, drive slowly and carefully, and follow the traffic rules. These precautions save the bones from fractures and injuries.

True Facts About the Body

  • The human body is composed of different parts.
  • The brain is protected by the skull.
  • We have 27 bones in one hand.
  • Ears are the organs of hearing, not of sight.
  • Cavities can develop in teeth if we do not brush them properly.

Key Points

  • Brush teeth twice a day to prevent cavities.
  • Exercise daily and eat less oily food for a healthy heart.
  • Always wear a helmet to protect the bones.
  • The brain is protected by the skull.

mcqs.q: Cavities and toothache are disorders of the:
mcqs.why: Disorders of the teeth are cavities and toothache. To prevent them we should brush our teeth twice a day and eat fewer sweet things.

mcqs.q: How can we prevent disorders of the teeth?
options: By brushing twice a day and eating fewer sweets
mcqs.why: We should brush our teeth twice a day and eat fewer sweet things to prevent cavities and toothache.

mcqs.q: Indigestion and stomach ache can be prevented by:
options: Eating clean and fresh food on time
mcqs.why: Disorders of the stomach are indigestion and stomach ache; we should eat clean and fresh food on time to prevent them.

mcqs.q: For a healthy heart we should:
options: Exercise daily and eat less oily food
mcqs.why: To prevent fast heartbeat and heart diseases, we should exercise daily and eat less oily food.

mcqs.q: Cough and difficulty in breathing are disorders of the:
mcqs.why: Disorders of the lungs are cough and difficulty in breathing; we should breathe in clean air and stay away from tobacco smoke.

mcqs.q: What should a motor cyclist always wear?
mcqs.why: Motor cyclists should always wear a helmet, drive slowly and carefully, and follow the traffic rules to safeguard their bones.

mcqs.q: Athletes safeguard their bones by:
options: Breaking the rules of the game
Warming up and wearing knee pads and elbow pads
mcqs.why: Athletes should warm up before playing, wear protective things such as knee pads and elbow pads, and follow the rules of the game.

mcqs.q: The brain is protected by the:
mcqs.why: The brain is protected by the skull. The skeleton protects delicate internal parts such as the brain, the heart and the lungs.

mcqs.q: How many bones are there in one hand?
mcqs.why: We have 27 bones in our one hand. This is one of the true facts about the human body given in this unit.

mcqs.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Ears are the organs of sight
Cavities develop if we brush our teeth properly
The human body is composed of different parts
The heart is protected by the skull
mcqs.why: The human body is composed of different parts. Ears are organs of hearing, and cavities develop when teeth are not brushed properly.

chapters.title: Characteristics and Needs of Living Things

lessons.title: Living and Non-Living Things
lessons.notes_html:
Living and Non-Living Things

Living things can grow and they need air, water and food. Non-living things cannot grow. A baby animal inherits qualities from its parents; for example, a baby elephant inherits qualities from the mother and father elephant.

Comparing Two Parrots

The green parrot and the white parrot are similar because both are parrots, both have feathers, a beak and two legs, both can fly, and both eat seeds and fruits. They are different because the first parrot is green with a red beak, while the second parrot is white and has a yellow crest on its head. The green parrot lives on trees; the white parrot can also be seen walking on the ground.

Key Points

  • Living things grow and need air.
  • Non-living things cannot grow.
  • Young ones inherit qualities from their parents.
  • Animals of the same kind have similarities and differences.

mcqs.q: Which of these is true about non-living things?
mcqs.why: Non-living things cannot grow. Growing is a characteristic of living things only.

mcqs.q: Living things need which of these?
mcqs.why: Living things need air. It is one of the basic needs of all living things, along with water and food.

mcqs.q: A baby elephant inherits its qualities from:
mcqs.why: A baby elephant inherits qualities from the mother elephant and the father elephant, not from the mother alone.

mcqs.q: How are the green parrot and the white parrot similar?
options: Both have feathers, a beak and two legs
Both live only on the ground
mcqs.why: Both are parrots, both have feathers, a beak and two legs, both can fly, and both eat seeds and fruits.

mcqs.q: What is different about the white parrot?
options: It has a yellow crest on its head
mcqs.why: The white parrot is white in colour and has a yellow crest on its head, while the green parrot has a red beak.

mcqs.q: What do both parrots eat?
mcqs.why: Both the green parrot and the white parrot eat seeds and fruits. This is one of their similarities.

mcqs.q: Which of these can grow?
mcqs.why: A plant is a living thing, so it can grow. Stones, chairs and books are non-living things and cannot grow.

mcqs.q: The green parrot lives mostly:
mcqs.why: The green parrot lives on trees, while the white parrot can also be seen walking on the ground.

mcqs.q: In the life cycle of a plant, which grows first?
options: The roots and shoot from the seed
mcqs.why: In the life cycle of a plant, the leaves do not grow first; first the seed germinates and the roots and shoot grow from it.

mcqs.q: Which statement is false?
options: Young ones inherit qualities from parents
mcqs.why: The statement that non-living things can grow is false, because only living things can grow.

lessons.title: Life Cycle of a Bean Plant
lessons.notes_html:
The Life Cycle of a Bean Plant

First the bean (seed) is sown in the soil. With water and warmth the bean germinates: the roots grow down into the soil and the stem and shoot grow upwards. Then the plant grows with new shoots and leaves. At last flowers appear on the plant, new beans are formed from them, and the life cycle starts again.

Observing a Sown Seed

  • After 3 days: the seed swells and a tiny white root begins to come out.
  • After 7 days: the root goes deeper into the soil and a small stem comes out of the ground.
  • After two weeks: the stem becomes bigger and the first green leaves appear.
  • After one month: the plant has grown quite big, with roots, a stem and many leaves.

Order of Germination

First there is the dry seed. Then the seed absorbs water, swells and its coat bursts. After that the root comes out and grows downwards. Then the stem grows upwards and the seed comes out of the ground. At last a small plant with roots, stem and leaves is formed.

Key Points

  • A seed needs water and warmth to germinate.
  • The root grows downwards and the stem grows upwards.
  • Flowers form new beans, and the cycle starts again.

mcqs.q: What does a bean seed need to germinate?
mcqs.why: With water and warmth the bean germinates; the roots grow down into the soil and the stem and shoot grow upwards.

mcqs.q: Which part of the germinating seed grows downwards?
mcqs.why: During germination the roots grow down into the soil, while the stem and shoot grow upwards towards the light.

mcqs.q: After 3 days of sowing, what is seen?
options: The seed swells and a tiny white root comes out
mcqs.why: After 3 days the seed swells and a tiny white root begins to come out of it. Leaves and flowers come much later.

mcqs.q: After 7 days of sowing, what happens?
options: The root goes deeper and a small stem comes out of the ground
mcqs.why: After 7 days the root goes deeper into the soil and a small stem comes out of the ground.

mcqs.q: When do the first green leaves appear on the young plant?
mcqs.why: After two weeks the stem becomes bigger and the first green leaves appear on the young plant.

mcqs.q: What is formed from the flowers of the bean plant?
mcqs.why: At last flowers appear on the plant and new beans are formed from them, and the life cycle starts again.

mcqs.q: What happens first when a dry seed is sown and watered?
options: The seed absorbs water, swells and its coat bursts
mcqs.why: First there is the dry seed; then the seed absorbs water, swells and its coat bursts, and after that the root comes out.

mcqs.q: After one month, the young plant has:
options: Roots, a stem and many leaves
mcqs.why: After one month the plant has grown quite big, with roots, a stem and many leaves.

mcqs.q: The process by which a seed starts to grow is called:
mcqs.why: Germination is the process in which a seed, with water and warmth, starts to grow into a new plant.

mcqs.q: In the life cycle, what comes just before flowers appear?
options: The plant grows with new shoots and leaves
mcqs.why: The plant first grows and its growth continues with new shoots and leaves; at last flowers appear on the plant.

lessons.title: Life Cycle of a Butterfly
lessons.notes_html:
The Life Cycle of a Butterfly

The life cycle of a butterfly has four stages: egg, larva (caterpillar), pupa and adult butterfly. In some days the larva becomes a pupa, and then a beautiful butterfly comes out of it.

Project: Observing a Larva

Place the larva and fresh leaves in an empty glass or plastic bottle and cover it with a lid having small holes. The holes in the lid are necessary so that the larva gets fresh air to breathe; otherwise it would die. Fresh leaves should be changed daily so that the larva keeps getting fresh leaves to eat.

Key Points

  • Stages: egg, larva, pupa, butterfly.
  • The larva needs fresh air to breathe.
  • The larva eats fresh leaves every day.

mcqs.q: What is the second stage in the life cycle of a butterfly?
mcqs.why: The stages are egg, larva (caterpillar), pupa and butterfly. The larva comes after the egg.

mcqs.q: The larva changes into which stage next?
mcqs.why: In some days the larva becomes a pupa, and then a beautiful butterfly comes out of the pupa.

mcqs.q: Why are holes necessary in the lid of the bottle?
options: So the larva can see outside
So the larva gets fresh air to breathe
So the butterfly can fly away
mcqs.why: The holes in the lid are necessary so that the larva gets fresh air to breathe; otherwise it would die.

mcqs.q: Why should the leaves in the bottle be changed daily?
options: So the larva keeps getting fresh leaves to eat
mcqs.why: Fresh leaves should be changed daily so that the larva keeps getting fresh leaves to eat.

mcqs.q: What does the larva eat?
mcqs.why: The larva is placed in the bottle with fresh leaves because it eats fresh leaves every day.

mcqs.q: Which stage comes out of the pupa?
mcqs.why: The larva becomes a pupa, and then a beautiful butterfly comes out of the pupa. The butterfly is the adult stage.

mcqs.q: How many stages are there in the life cycle of a butterfly?
mcqs.why: There are four stages: egg, larva (caterpillar), pupa and butterfly.

mcqs.q: Where should the bottle with the larva be kept?
mcqs.why: The bottle is covered with the lid having holes and kept in an airy place so the larva can breathe and live.

mcqs.q: The larva of a butterfly is also called a:
mcqs.why: The larva stage of a butterfly is also called a caterpillar. It later changes into a pupa.

mcqs.q: What comes first in the butterfly's life cycle?
mcqs.why: The life cycle begins with the egg. From the egg comes the larva, then the pupa, and then the butterfly.

lessons.title: Food Groups and Nutrients
lessons.notes_html:
Proteins

The main sources of protein are meat, milk, eggs, fish, pulses and peas. Proteins are very necessary for the growth of the body and for repairing its worn-out parts. A ruptured skin requires protein-rich food for its repair.

Fats and Carbohydrates

Similarities: both give us energy and both are a part of our daily diet. Differences: carbohydrates give us quick energy and are obtained from grains, sugar and bread, while fats store energy and give warmth to the body and are obtained from oil, butter and ghee.

Vitamins and Minerals

Similarities: both do not give us energy, but both are necessary for health and both are needed in small amounts. Differences: vitamins are obtained from fruits and vegetables and protect the body from diseases, while minerals such as salt and calcium are obtained from milk, meat and vegetables and help in the growth of bones and teeth.

Key Points

  • Proteins help in growth and repair of the body.
  • Carbohydrates give quick energy; fats store energy and give warmth.
  • Vitamins and minerals do not give energy but are necessary for health.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a main source of protein?
mcqs.why: The main sources of protein are meat, milk, eggs, fish, pulses and peas. Sugar, oil and bread are not protein sources.

mcqs.q: Proteins are necessary for the body because they help in:
options: Growth and repair of worn-out parts
mcqs.why: Proteins are very necessary for the growth of the body and for repairing its worn-out parts, such as a ruptured skin.

mcqs.q: Carbohydrates give us:
mcqs.why: Carbohydrates give us quick energy and are obtained from grains, sugar and bread.

mcqs.q: Fats are obtained from:
mcqs.why: Fats store energy and give warmth to the body, and they are obtained from oil, butter and ghee.

mcqs.q: What is similar between fats and carbohydrates?
options: Both are needed in small amounts only
mcqs.why: Both fats and carbohydrates give us energy and both are a part of our daily diet. This is their similarity.

mcqs.q: Vitamins are obtained mainly from:
mcqs.why: Vitamins are obtained from fruits and vegetables and they protect the body from diseases.

mcqs.q: Which of these is true about vitamins and minerals?
options: They give us a lot of energy
They do not provide energy but are important for health
They are not needed by the body
They are obtained only from meat
mcqs.why: Vitamins do not provide energy but are important for health. The same is true of minerals; both are needed in small amounts.

mcqs.q: Minerals such as calcium help in the growth of:
mcqs.why: Minerals such as salt and calcium are obtained from milk, meat and vegetables and help in the growth of bones and teeth.

mcqs.q: Which food is a source of protein from plants?
mcqs.why: Pulses and peas are plant sources of protein, while meat, milk, eggs and fish are animal sources.

mcqs.q: Fats differ from carbohydrates because fats:
options: Store energy and give warmth to the body
mcqs.why: Fats store energy and give warmth to the body, while carbohydrates give quick energy. This is the main difference between them.

lessons.title: Balanced Diet and the Food Pyramid
lessons.notes_html:
Balanced Diet

A balanced diet includes food from all the food groups in the right amounts. The food groups include grains, fruits, vegetables, dairy, and meat and pulses.

The Food Pyramid

A Food Pyramid Chart helps one to choose suitable food daily. A food pyramid helps us prepare a balanced diet plan for three reasons:

  • First, the pyramid tells us how much food of each group should be eaten daily.
  • Second, with its help we can include food from all the groups in our diet, and no group is left out.
  • Third, with its help we can avoid eating too much or too little and can prepare a healthy and balanced diet.

Sources of Food

We get food from plant sources (grains, pulses, vegetables and fruits) and from animal sources (milk, eggs, meat and fish). We eat plant food the most, especially grains such as rice and wheat roti.

Key Points

  • A balanced diet has food from all food groups.
  • The food pyramid tells us how much of each group to eat daily.
  • Grains are the food we eat the most.

mcqs.q: A balanced diet includes:
options: Food from all the food groups
mcqs.why: A balanced diet includes food from all the food groups: grains, fruits, vegetables, dairy, and meat and pulses.

mcqs.q: A Food Pyramid Chart helps one to:
mcqs.why: A Food Pyramid Chart helps one in choosing suitable food daily. This statement is true.

mcqs.q: The first reason the food pyramid helps is that it tells us:
options: How much food of each group should be eaten daily
mcqs.why: The pyramid tells us how much food of each group should be eaten daily, so we can plan a balanced diet.

mcqs.q: With the help of the pyramid, we can avoid:
options: Eating too much or too little
mcqs.why: With the help of the pyramid we can avoid eating too much or too little and can prepare a healthy and balanced diet.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a plant source of food?
mcqs.why: Grains come from plants. Milk, eggs and fish are animal sources of food.

mcqs.q: Which food do we eat the most?
options: Grains such as rice and wheat roti
mcqs.why: We eat plant food the most, especially grains such as rice and wheat roti, because they are included in every meal.

mcqs.q: Which food do we eat the least?
mcqs.why: We eat fish the least, because it is not available daily in our area and it is also rather expensive.

mcqs.q: Which of these belongs to the dairy group?
mcqs.why: Milk belongs to the dairy group. Bread is a grain, apple is a fruit and peas give protein.

mcqs.q: In a three-day balanced plan, the three days together should include:
mcqs.why: Each day should include food from at least three food groups, and the three days together should include food from every food group.

mcqs.q: Which statement is false?
options: A balanced diet includes food from all groups
Half of our daily diet in winter should be fat
The food pyramid helps choose food daily
mcqs.why: It is false that in winter half portion of our daily diet should comprise fat. A balanced diet has the right amount of each group.

lessons.title: Unbalanced Diet and Planning a Balanced Meal
lessons.notes_html:
Effects of an Unbalanced Diet

  • First effect: the body becomes weak and we get tired quickly.
  • Second effect: the growth of children stops and they fall ill easily.
  • Third effect: the shortage of any one substance can cause special diseases, such as weak eyesight due to shortage of vitamins and shortage of blood due to shortage of iron.

Planning a Balanced Diet

A sample plan: Day 1: milk and roti in breakfast, rice and pulses in lunch, vegetable and roti at night, with a banana. Day 2: egg and milk in breakfast, meat and roti in lunch, pulses and vegetable at night, with an apple. Day 3: porridge and milk in breakfast, fish and rice in lunch, peas and roti at night, with an orange. Add clean water and milk as drinks every day.

Key Points

  • An unbalanced diet makes the body weak.
  • Shortage of vitamins causes weak eyesight.
  • Shortage of iron causes shortage of blood.
  • Every meal plan should include food from different groups.

mcqs.q: What is the first effect of eating an unbalanced diet?
options: The body becomes weak and we get tired quickly
mcqs.why: The first effect of an unbalanced diet is that the body becomes weak and we get tired quickly.

mcqs.q: An unbalanced diet can stop which of these in children?
mcqs.why: The second effect is that the growth of children stops and they fall ill easily.

mcqs.q: Weak eyesight can be caused by the shortage of:
mcqs.why: The shortage of vitamins can cause weak eyesight. Shortage of one substance causes special diseases.

mcqs.q: Shortage of blood is caused by the shortage of:
mcqs.why: Shortage of blood is due to the shortage of iron in the diet. Iron is a mineral needed by the body.

mcqs.q: Children who eat an unbalanced diet:
mcqs.why: With an unbalanced diet, the growth of children stops and they fall ill easily.

mcqs.q: In the sample plan, breakfast on Day 2 is:
mcqs.why: In the sample three-day plan, Day 2 breakfast is egg and milk, lunch is meat and roti, and night meal is pulses and vegetable.

mcqs.q: Which drink should be added every day in a balanced plan?
mcqs.why: Clean water and milk should be added as drinks every day to make the diet plan complete and balanced.

mcqs.q: A balanced meal plan includes both:
options: Plant and animal sources of food
mcqs.why: In the plan we include both plant sources (grains, pulses, vegetables, fruits) and animal sources (milk, eggs, meat, fish).

mcqs.q: What happens if any one food substance is missing from the diet?
mcqs.why: The shortage of any one substance can cause special diseases, such as weak eyesight from shortage of vitamins.

mcqs.q: Which meal in the sample plan includes fish?
mcqs.why: On Day 3, lunch is fish and rice, breakfast is porridge and milk, and the night meal is peas and roti with an orange.

lessons.title: Living and Non-Living Components of the Environment
lessons.notes_html:
The Environment

Everything around us is a part of the environment. The environment has living components and non-living components. Living components include plants, animals and human beings. Non-living components include air, water, soil, rocks and sunlight. All living things depend on these non-living components for their life.

Types of Environment

  • Land is not a living component of the environment.
  • A wetland is a water environment.
  • Grasslands do not have many trees.
  • Plants with needle-like leaves belong to cold or mountain environments, not to the desert.

Common and Different

All environments have both living and non-living components. But the weather, the amount of water and the kind of land are different in every environment, so the plants and animals of each environment are also different, such as the camel and cactus in the desert and fishes in water.

Key Points

  • Living components: plants, animals, human beings.
  • Non-living components: air, water, soil, rocks, sunlight.
  • Every environment has both kinds of components.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a living component of the environment?
mcqs.why: Living components include plants, animals and human beings. Soil, rocks and sunlight are non-living components.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT a living component of the land environment?
mcqs.why: An iron rock is a non-living component. Flowering plants, frogs and human beings are living components.

mcqs.q: Land is:
options: Not a living component of the environment
mcqs.why: The statement 'Land is not a living component of the environment' is true. Land is a non-living component.

mcqs.q: A wetland is which type of environment?
mcqs.why: A wetland is a water environment. The statement given in the review questions is true.

mcqs.q: Which of these is not a type of environment?
mcqs.why: A storeroom is not a type of environment. Gardens and ponds are environments where living things live.

mcqs.q: Grasslands have:
mcqs.why: The statement 'Grasslands have many trees' is false. Grasslands have grasses and not many trees.

mcqs.q: What is common in all environments?
mcqs.why: All environments have both living and non-living components, and all living things depend on one another for life.

mcqs.q: What is different in all environments?
options: The weather, the amount of water and the kind of land
mcqs.why: The weather, the amount of water and the kind of land are different in every environment, so their plants and animals are also different.

mcqs.q: The camel and the cactus are found in the:
mcqs.why: The camel and cactus live in the desert. Their characteristics are according to their environment, just as fishes live in water.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a non-living component?
mcqs.why: Non-living components include air, water, soil, rocks and sunlight. Plants, animals and human beings are living components.

lessons.title: Food Chains: Producers, Consumers and Decomposers
lessons.notes_html:
Food Chains

All food chains start with the Sun. Plants make their own food, so they are called producers. Animals cannot make their own food; they eat other living things, so they are consumers. The correct order of levels in a food chain is: Producer, Consumer, Decomposer.

Kinds of Consumers

  • Herbivores eat plants only.
  • Carnivores eat other animals.
  • Omnivores eat both plants and animals. Human beings are omnivores.
  • Animals that eat herbivores are secondary consumers.

A Simple Food Chain

Sun, Plant (producer), Frog (consumer), Snake (consumer), Hawk (consumer). In this chain, if the number of frogs increased, the plants would decrease, because the frogs feed on the level below them in the chain.

Decomposers

Decomposers, such as mould, break down dead plants and animals into small substances which mix into the soil. This makes the soil fertile and plants get the substances they need for growth. Without decomposers, dead bodies would keep collecting and the land would fill with waste.

Key Points

  • All food chains start with the Sun.
  • Plants are producers; animals are consumers.
  • Decomposers break down dead plants and animals.
  • Human beings are omnivores.

mcqs.q: All food chains start with the:
mcqs.why: All food chains start with the Sun, because plants use sunlight to make their food.

mcqs.q: Plants are called producers because they:
mcqs.why: Plants make their own food with the help of sunlight, so they are called producers in the food chain.

mcqs.q: A frog is best described as a:
mcqs.why: A frog cannot make its own food; it eats other living things, so it is a consumer.

mcqs.q: What is the correct order of the levels in a food chain?
mcqs.why: The correct order is Producer, Consumer, Decomposer. Producers make food, consumers eat it and decomposers break down the dead.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is a decomposer?
mcqs.why: Mould is a decomposer. Decomposers break down dead plants and animals into small substances that mix into the soil.

mcqs.q: Human beings are placed in the group of:
mcqs.why: Human beings eat both plants and animals, so they are omnivores.

mcqs.q: Animals that eat herbivores are called:
mcqs.why: Animals that eat herbivores are secondary consumers. The statement that animals eating carnivores are secondary consumers is false.

mcqs.q: The key role of decomposers is to:
options: Break down dead animals and plants
mcqs.why: Decomposers break down dead plants and animals into small substances, which mix into the soil and make it fertile.

mcqs.q: In the food chain Sun-Plant-Frog-Snake-Hawk, which living thing would decrease if the number of frogs increased?
mcqs.why: In the given food chain the answer is plants: the level below the frogs in the chain is eaten more as frogs increase in number.

mcqs.q: Herbivores are animals that eat:
mcqs.why: Herbivores eat plants only. The statement 'Herbivores eat plant and animals' is false; animals eating both are omnivores.

lessons.title: How Living Things Depend on Each Other
lessons.notes_html:
Plants and Animals Need Each Other

Plants give food and oxygen to animals and also give a home to many animals. On the other hand, animals give carbon dioxide to plants and help in spreading their seeds and in the pollination of flowers. That is why both cannot live without each other.

Changes Made by Humans

Humans have cut trees and finished forests, made air and water dirty with the smoke of factories and vehicles, and reduced the homes of animals by building cities and roads. Due to these changes many animals and plants have come in danger. We should plant trees, reduce waste and protect the environment.

Key Points

  • Plants give food, oxygen and homes to animals.
  • Animals give carbon dioxide to plants and spread their seeds.
  • Humans have damaged the environment by cutting forests and polluting air and water.
  • We should plant trees and protect the environment.

mcqs.q: Plants give which of these to animals?
mcqs.why: Plants give food and oxygen to animals and also give a home to many animals.

mcqs.q: Animals give which gas to plants?
mcqs.why: Animals give carbon dioxide to plants, which plants use to make their food. Animals also help in spreading seeds and pollination.

mcqs.q: How do animals help flowers?
mcqs.why: Animals help in the pollination of flowers and in spreading the seeds of plants to new places.

mcqs.q: Why are decomposers an important part of the food chain?
options: They make the soil fertile by breaking down dead bodies
They eat all the waste plastic
mcqs.why: Decomposers break down dead plants and animals into small substances which mix into the soil, making it fertile for plants.

mcqs.q: What would happen if there were no decomposers?
options: Dead bodies would keep collecting and the land would fill with waste
mcqs.why: If there were no decomposers, dead bodies would keep collecting and the land would fill with waste.

mcqs.q: Which change have humans introduced in the environment?
options: They cut trees and made air and water dirty
They increased the homes of animals
mcqs.why: Humans have cut trees and finished forests, and made air and water dirty with the smoke of factories and vehicles.

mcqs.q: Building cities and roads has:
mcqs.why: Humans have reduced the homes of animals by building cities and roads, so many animals and plants have come in danger.

mcqs.q: What should we do to protect the environment?
options: Plant trees, reduce waste and protect the environment
mcqs.why: We should plant trees, reduce waste and protect the environment so that plants and animals stay safe.

mcqs.q: Plants and animals are important for each other because:
options: They live in the same zoo
Each gives things the other needs to live
mcqs.why: Plants give food, oxygen and homes to animals, while animals give carbon dioxide and spread seeds, so both cannot live without each other.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a home that plants give to animals?
options: Trees where birds and animals live
mcqs.why: Plants, especially trees, give a home to many animals and birds, besides giving food and oxygen.

lessons.title: Solids, Liquids and Gases
lessons.notes_html:
What is Matter?

Anything that has mass and occupies space is matter. All forms of matter — solids, liquids and gases — have mass and occupy space.

The Three States

  • A solid, like a book, has mass and occupies space on the table. Solids do not take the shape of the container they are kept in.
  • A liquid, like milk, has mass and occupies space in the glass. Liquids take the shape of the container they are placed in.
  • A gas, like the air inside a balloon, also has a little mass and occupies all the space of the balloon. Gases change volume when transferred from a small ball to a large ball.

Key Points

  • Matter has mass and occupies space.
  • Solids keep their own shape.
  • Liquids take the shape of their container.
  • Gases spread out to fill the whole space.

mcqs.q: Anything that has mass and occupies space is called:
mcqs.why: Anything that has mass and occupies space is matter. A book, milk and the air in a balloon are all examples of matter.

mcqs.q: Which state of matter does NOT take the shape of its container?
mcqs.why: Solids do not take the shape of the container they are kept in. This statement is true, while liquids do take the shape of the container.

mcqs.q: Liquids take the shape of:
options: The container they are placed in
mcqs.why: Liquids take the shape of the container they are placed in, for example milk takes the shape of the glass.

mcqs.q: The air inside a balloon is an example of:
mcqs.why: The air inside a balloon is a gas; it also has a little mass and occupies all the space of the balloon.

mcqs.q: When a gas is transferred from a small ball to a large ball, it:
mcqs.why: Gases change volume when transferred from a small ball to a large ball; they spread out to fill the whole space.

mcqs.q: Which of these has mass and occupies space?
options: All of them: book, milk and air
mcqs.why: All forms of matter have mass and occupy space: a book is a solid, milk is a liquid and air is a gas.

mcqs.q: Milk in a glass is an example of:
mcqs.why: Milk is a liquid; it has mass and occupies space in the glass, and it takes the shape of the glass.

mcqs.q: Which statement is true?
options: Solids take the shape of the container
Liquids take the shape of the container they are placed in
mcqs.why: Liquids take the shape of a container they are placed in. Solids keep their shape and all matter has mass.

mcqs.q: A book on a table shows that a solid:
mcqs.why: A book is a solid; it has mass and it occupies space on the table.

mcqs.q: How many states of matter are described in this unit?
mcqs.why: There are three states of matter: solid, liquid and gas. All three have mass and occupy space.

lessons.title: Changing States of Matter
lessons.notes_html:
Ice Changes to Water

Ice is the solid form of water. When we heat ice, it melts and changes into water, because with heat its particles become loose and start flowing. An ice lolly and ice cream melt when kept in a warm place.

Gas Changes into Liquid

When a gas is cooled, it changes into a liquid; this process is called condensation. Drops of water appear on the outer side of a cold glass, because the water vapours present in the air touch the cold surface and change into water. Dew in winter is also formed in the same way.

Matter Changes Its State on Heating

Ice (solid) changes into water (liquid), and water changes into steam (gas) on heating.

Key Points

  • Ice melts into water on heating.
  • Water changes into steam on heating.
  • A gas changes into a liquid on cooling — this is condensation.
  • Dew is formed by condensation.

mcqs.q: Ice is the solid form of:
mcqs.why: Ice is the solid form of water. When we heat ice, it melts and changes into water.

mcqs.q: When ice is heated, it:
mcqs.why: When we heat ice, it melts and changes into water, because with heat its particles become loose and start flowing.

mcqs.q: The process by which a gas changes into a liquid is called:
mcqs.why: When a gas is cooled, it changes into a liquid; this process is called condensation.

mcqs.q: Drops of water on the outer side of a cold glass are formed because:
options: Water vapours in the air touch the cold surface and change into water
The glass is wet from inside
mcqs.why: The water vapours present in the air touch the cold surface of the glass and change into water. This is condensation.

mcqs.q: Dew in winter is formed by:
mcqs.why: Dew in winter is formed in the same way as drops on a cold glass — by the condensation of water vapours in the air.

mcqs.q: On heating, water changes into:
mcqs.why: Matter changes its state on heating: ice (solid) changes to water (liquid) and water changes to steam (gas).

mcqs.q: An ice lolly kept in a warm place will:
mcqs.why: An ice lolly and ice cream melt when kept in a warm place, because heat makes the particles of ice loose and flowing.

mcqs.q: Why do the particles of ice start flowing on heating?
mcqs.why: With heat, the particles of ice become loose and start flowing, so the ice melts and changes into water.

mcqs.q: To change a gas into a liquid, we should:
mcqs.why: When a gas is cooled, it changes into a liquid. Cooling causes condensation, as seen on a cold glass.

mcqs.q: The correct order of states on heating ice is:
mcqs.why: On heating, ice (solid) first changes into water (liquid), and water then changes into steam (gas).

lessons.title: Dissolving and Separating Mixtures
lessons.notes_html:
Soluble and Insoluble Solids

When we mix sugar in water, it dissolves completely in it and disappears; it is a soluble solid. Plastic pieces do not dissolve in water and, being light, they keep floating on the surface of the water; they are insoluble solids.

Filtration

Tea leaves can be separated from tea by filtration. But solids that dissolve in water cannot be separated through filtration, because they pass through the filter with the water.

Project: Separating Salt, Sand and Tea Leaves

  • First sieve the mixture; the large tea leaves stay in the sieve and the salt and sand pass down.
  • Then mix the salt and sand in water; the salt dissolves and the sand does not.
  • Then filter it through a cloth or filter paper; the sand stays in the filter and the salty water comes down.
  • At last heat the salty water so the water evaporates away, and white salt is left in the dish.

Key Points

  • Sugar is soluble; plastic is insoluble and floats.
  • Tea leaves are separated by filtration.
  • Dissolved solids are recovered by evaporating the water.

mcqs.q: Sugar mixed in water is an example of a:
mcqs.why: When we mix sugar in water, it dissolves completely in it and disappears; sugar is a soluble solid.

mcqs.q: Plastic pieces in water:
options: Do not dissolve and keep floating on the surface
mcqs.why: Plastic pieces do not dissolve in water and, being light, they keep floating on the surface; they are insoluble solids.

mcqs.q: Tea leaves can be separated from tea by:
mcqs.why: Tea leaves can be separated from tea by filtration. The statement given in the review questions is true.

mcqs.q: A solid that has dissolved in water can be separated by filtration:
options: No, because it passes through the filter with the water
mcqs.why: The statement 'Solids that dissolve in water can be separated through filtration' is false, because the dissolved solid passes through with the water.

mcqs.q: In the project, the first step to separate tea leaves from salt and sand is to:
mcqs.why: First sieve the mixture; the large tea leaves will stay in the sieve and the salt and sand will pass down.

mcqs.q: After sieving, the salt and sand are mixed in water so that:
options: The salt dissolves and the sand does not
mcqs.why: The salt dissolves in the water and the sand does not dissolve, so the two can then be separated by filtration.

mcqs.q: During filtration of the salt-sand-water mixture:
options: The salt stays in the filter
The sand stays in the filter and salty water comes down
The water stays in the filter
mcqs.why: The mixture is filtered through a cloth or filter paper; the sand stays in the filter and the salty water comes down.

mcqs.q: How is the salt finally recovered from the salty water?
options: By heating the water so it evaporates away
mcqs.why: At last heat the salty water so that the water evaporates away, and white salt will be left in the dish.

mcqs.q: Which of these will float on water?
mcqs.why: Plastic pieces are insoluble and light, so they keep floating on the surface of the water.

mcqs.q: Which method is used to separate the sand in the project?
mcqs.why: The sand is separated by filtration through a cloth or filter paper, while sieving separates the tea leaves and heating recovers the salt.

lessons.title: Heat and Temperature
lessons.notes_html:
Heat

Heat is a form of energy which flows from a hot object to a cold object. The properties used for heat are: hot, energy and cold.

Temperature

Temperature tells us how hot or cold an object is. It is measured with a thermometer. It is not correct to say that heat tells us how hot an object is — that is the work of temperature. Temperature does not flow; it is heat that flows from a higher temperature region to a lower temperature region.

Similarities and Differences

  • Similarities: both heat and temperature are related to each other and both are about an object being hot or cold.
  • Differences: heat is a form of energy which flows from a hot object to a cold object, while temperature tells us how hot or cold an object is and is measured with a thermometer.

Key Points

  • Heat is a form of energy.
  • Temperature tells how hot or cold an object is.
  • Temperature is measured with a thermometer.

mcqs.q: Heat is a form of:
mcqs.why: Heat is a form of energy which flows from a hot object to a cold object. The properties used for heat are hot, energy and cold.

mcqs.q: Temperature tells us:
options: How hot or cold an object is
mcqs.why: Temperature tells us how hot or cold an object is, and it is measured with a thermometer.

mcqs.q: Temperature is measured with a:
mcqs.why: Temperature is measured with a thermometer, while heat is the energy that flows from a hot object to a cold one.

mcqs.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Heat tells us how hot an object is
Temperature flows from one body to another
Heat flows from a hot object to a cold object
Temperature is a form of energy
mcqs.why: Heat flows from a hot object to a cold object. Saying 'heat tells us how hot an object is' is false — that is temperature's work.

mcqs.q: The properties used for heat are:
mcqs.why: The properties used for heat are: hot, energy, cold. Colour, smell and sound are not properties of heat.

mcqs.q: How are heat and temperature similar?
options: Both are about an object being hot or cold
mcqs.why: Both are related to each other and both are about an object being hot or cold. This is their similarity.

mcqs.q: Heat flows from:
options: A cold object to a hot object
A hot object to a cold object
mcqs.why: Heat is a form of energy which always flows from a hot object to a cold object, that is, from higher temperature to lower temperature.

mcqs.q: Which statement is false?
options: Temperature flows from higher region to lower region
Heat is a form of energy
Temperature is measured with a thermometer
Heat flows from hot to cold
mcqs.why: The statement 'Temperature flows from higher region to lower region' is false. It is heat that flows, not temperature.

mcqs.q: If an object feels very hot, it has a:
mcqs.why: Temperature tells us how hot or cold an object is, so a very hot object has a high temperature.

mcqs.q: Which instrument would you use to know the temperature of water?
mcqs.why: A thermometer is the instrument used to measure temperature, such as the temperature of water in a beaker.

lessons.title: Thermometers
lessons.notes_html:
Clinical Thermometer

The clinical thermometer is used to measure body temperature. The liquid used in it is mercury. Normal body temperature is 98.4 °F or 37 °C. There is a constriction in the clinical thermometer which helps in preventing the flow of mercury downwards, so the reading stays. Its highest temperature is not 32 °C.

Laboratory Thermometer

The laboratory thermometer is used to measure the temperature of things like water in beakers. Its lowest temperature is -10 °C.

Handling a Clinical Thermometer

Wash it before use and place it in its cover after use. Stay at one place while using it. Do NOT run while handling a clinical thermometer.

Make Your Own Thermometer (Project)

Fill a narrow-necked plastic bottle up to one fourth with equal amounts of water and rubbing alcohol, and add two drops of red food colour. Put a clear plastic straw in the bottle so its lower end does not touch the bottom, and seal the mouth with modelling clay, keeping the top of the straw open. When you warm the bottle with your hands, the mixture rises up in the straw; at a cold place it comes down. In this way it shows the change of temperature.

Key Points

  • Mercury is used in a clinical thermometer.
  • Normal body temperature is 37 °C (98.4 °F).
  • The constriction stops the mercury from flowing back down.
  • Do not run while handling a clinical thermometer.

mcqs.q: Which liquid is used in a clinical thermometer?
mcqs.why: Mercury is the liquid used in the clinical thermometer. It rises when the thermometer touches the warm body.

mcqs.q: Normal body temperature is:
mcqs.why: Normal body temperature is 98.4 °F or 37 °C. The temperature of healthy people remains about 37 °C.

mcqs.q: The lowest temperature in a laboratory thermometer is:
mcqs.why: The lowest temperature in a laboratory thermometer is -10 °C, so it can measure temperatures below zero as well.

mcqs.q: The constriction in a clinical thermometer helps in:
options: Preventing the flow of mercury downwards
mcqs.why: The constriction in the clinical thermometer helps in preventing the flow of mercury downwards, so we can read the temperature easily.

mcqs.q: What should you NOT do while handling a clinical thermometer?
mcqs.why: You should not run while handling a clinical thermometer, because it can break. Wash it before use and place it in its cover after use.

mcqs.q: The statement 'The highest temperature in a clinical thermometer is 32 °C' is:
mcqs.why: This statement is false. A clinical thermometer must measure body temperature around 37 °C, so its range goes above 32 °C.

mcqs.q: In the activity, the temperature of beakers is measured with a:
mcqs.why: The temperature of the three beakers is measured with a laboratory thermometer, and body temperature with a clinical thermometer.

mcqs.q: In the home-made thermometer project, the coloured mixture rises in the straw when:
options: The bottle is warmed with the hands
mcqs.why: When you warm the bottle with your hands, the mixture gets warm and rises up in the straw; at a cold place it comes down.

mcqs.q: Which beaker showed the highest temperature in the activity?
options: The beaker with icy cold water
mcqs.why: The beaker with hot water showed the highest temperature and the beaker with icy cold water showed the lowest temperature.

mcqs.q: The body temperature of every healthy person remains about:
mcqs.why: The body temperature of every person can be a little different, but the temperature of healthy people remains about 37 °C.

lessons.title: Direction of Heat Flow
lessons.notes_html:
Heat Always Flows from Hot to Cold

Heat always flows from a higher temperature to a lower temperature. Arrows are drawn from the hotter object outwards towards the colder surroundings.

Examples

  • Tea in a cup is at 70 °C and the surroundings are at 0 °C: heat flows from the tea to the surroundings, and with time the tea becomes cold.
  • Juice in a glass is at 5 °C and the surroundings are at 0 °C: heat still flows from the juice to the surroundings, because 5 °C is higher than 0 °C, although the difference is small.
  • A heater is at 200 °C: heat flows from the heater to the cold air of the room in all directions, so the whole room becomes warm.
  • The Sun's surface is at 5,500 °C: heat flows from the Sun outwards into space and towards the Earth, giving us light and warmth.

Key Points

  • Heat flows from higher temperature to lower temperature.
  • Even a small difference makes heat flow.
  • The Sun's heat spreads in all directions.

mcqs.q: Heat always flows from:
mcqs.why: Heat always flows from higher temperature to lower temperature, that is, from a hot object to a cold object.

mcqs.q: Tea at 70 °C is kept in surroundings of 0 °C. Heat will flow:
options: From the surroundings to the tea
From the tea to the surroundings
mcqs.why: Heat will flow from the tea to the surroundings, because the tea is much hotter. With time the tea becomes cold.

mcqs.q: Juice at 5 °C is kept in surroundings of 0 °C. What happens?
options: Heat flows from the juice to the surroundings
No heat flows because 5 °C is cold
mcqs.why: Heat will flow from the juice to the surroundings, because 5 °C is higher than 0 °C. Although the difference is small, heat always flows from higher to lower temperature.

mcqs.q: A heater at 200 °C warms a room because:
options: Cold air flows into the heater
Heat flows from the heater to the cold air in all directions
The room gives heat to the heater
mcqs.why: Heat flows from the heater to the cold air of the room and to the surroundings, so the whole room becomes warm.

mcqs.q: The temperature at the Sun's surface is about:
mcqs.why: The temperature at the Sun's surface is 5,500 degrees Celsius. Its heat flows outwards into space and towards the Earth.

mcqs.q: The Sun's heat reaches the Earth because heat flows:
options: From the Sun outwards towards the things around it
From the Earth to the Sun
mcqs.why: The Sun is the hottest of all, so its heat spreads in all directions and gives light and warmth to the Earth.

mcqs.q: If two objects have exactly the same temperature, heat flow between them is:
options: Stopped, because there is no temperature difference
From the bigger to the smaller
mcqs.why: Heat flows only from higher temperature to lower temperature. With no difference in temperature, heat does not flow.

mcqs.q: With time, hot tea in a cold room will:
options: Become cold as its heat flows out
mcqs.why: Heat flows from the tea to the surroundings, so with time the tea becomes cold and its temperature decreases.

mcqs.q: In the figures of this unit, arrows for heat flow are drawn:
mcqs.why: Arrows are drawn from the tea, heater or Sun outwards, because heat flows from a hot object to a cold object.

mcqs.q: Which pair shows the correct direction of heat flow?
options: From 200 °C heater to cold room air
From cold juice to hot tea
From the Earth to the Sun's surface
mcqs.why: Heat flows from the 200 °C heater to the cold air of the room. In all other pairs the direction would be from cold to hot, which never happens.

lessons.title: Force and Its Effects
lessons.notes_html:
What is Force?

A force is a push or a pull — but force is not only a push; it can also be a pull. When we move, we do one kind of work or the other. A machine makes work easier.

Effects of Force

  • Force can make a standing object start moving.
  • Force can make a moving object fast, slow or stop.
  • Force can change the direction of movement, just as kicking a football sends it to another side.
  • An object changes its shape when force is applied.
  • Force cannot change the mass of an object.

Friction and Gravity

Friction is always in the opposing direction to any ongoing action. The force that pulls everything towards the Earth is called gravitational force. It is because of this force that everything falls down to the Earth and we can stand on the Earth.

Key Points

  • Force can change speed, direction and shape.
  • Force cannot change mass.
  • Friction always opposes movement.
  • Gravity pulls everything towards the Earth.

mcqs.q: Force can bring all of the following changes in an object EXCEPT:
mcqs.why: Force can change the speed, direction and shape of an object, but it cannot change the mass of an object.

mcqs.q: The force that pulls everything towards the Earth is called:
mcqs.why: The force that pulls everything towards the Earth is called gravitational force. Because of it, everything falls down to the Earth.

mcqs.q: Friction always acts:
options: In the opposing direction to any ongoing action
mcqs.why: Friction is always in the opposing direction to any ongoing action. It opposes the movement of objects.

mcqs.q: When a football is kicked to another side, force has changed its:
mcqs.why: With force, the direction of movement of an object can also change, just as kicking a football sends it to another side.

mcqs.q: Which statement is true?
options: The direction of an object cannot be changed by force
mcqs.why: A machine makes work easier — this is true. Force is a push or a pull, and force can change direction but not mass.

mcqs.q: An object changes its shape when:
mcqs.why: An object changes its shape when force is applied, for example when clay or dough is pressed.

mcqs.q: Why do things fall down to the Earth?
mcqs.why: It is because of gravitational force that everything falls down to the Earth and we can stand on the Earth.

mcqs.q: A moving object can be stopped by:
mcqs.why: When force is applied, a moving object can become fast, slow or stop. Force is the cause of every kind of change in movement.

mcqs.q: Which statement is false?
options: A wheelbarrow is a simple machine
Speed is the rate of change of distance with time
mcqs.why: The statement 'Force is only a push' is false, because force can be a push or a pull.

mcqs.q: When we move from one place to another, we are:
options: Doing one kind of work or the other
mcqs.why: When we move, we do one kind of work or the other. Movement and work need force.

lessons.title: Speed
lessons.notes_html:
What is Speed?

Speed is defined as the rate of change of distance with time. To find the speed, the distance is divided by the time taken.

Worked Examples

  • A train travels a distance of 12 kilometres in 2 hours. Speed = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 kilometres per hour.
  • A girl walks 150 metres in 5 seconds. Speed = 150 ÷ 5 = 30 metres per second.

Key Points

  • Speed = distance ÷ time.
  • Speed is measured in kilometres per hour or metres per second.

mcqs.q: Speed is defined as:
options: The rate of change of distance with time
mcqs.why: Speed is defined as the rate of change of distance with time. To find speed, distance is divided by time.

mcqs.q: A train travels 12 kilometres in 2 hours. Its speed is:
mcqs.why: Speed = distance ÷ time = 12 kilometres ÷ 2 hours = 6. So the speed of the train is 6 kilometres per hour.

mcqs.q: A girl walks 150 metres in 5 seconds. Her speed is:
mcqs.why: Speed = 150 metres ÷ 5 seconds = 30. So her speed is 30 metres per second.

mcqs.q: To find the speed of an object, we divide:
mcqs.why: To find the speed, the distance is divided by the time, as in 12 kilometres divided by 2 hours gives 6 km/h.

mcqs.q: A car covers 100 kilometres in 2 hours. Its speed is:
mcqs.why: Speed = distance ÷ time = 100 ÷ 2 = 50 kilometres per hour. The same rule is used as in the train example.

mcqs.q: If a cyclist covers more distance in the same time, his speed is:
mcqs.why: Speed is the rate of change of distance with time, so covering more distance in the same time means greater speed.

mcqs.q: A boy runs 60 metres in 10 seconds. His speed is:
mcqs.why: Speed = 60 metres ÷ 10 seconds = 6 metres per second, using the same rule: distance divided by time.

mcqs.q: Which unit is used for the speed of the train in this unit?
mcqs.why: The train's speed is given in kilometres per hour (6 km/h), because its distance was in kilometres and time in hours.

mcqs.q: An object that does not move has speed:
mcqs.why: If an object covers no distance, its speed is zero, because speed is the rate of change of distance with time.

mcqs.q: A bus travels 90 kilometres in 3 hours. Its speed is:
mcqs.why: Speed = 90 kilometres ÷ 3 hours = 30 kilometres per hour. Distance is always divided by time to find speed.

lessons.title: Simple Machines
lessons.notes_html:
What are Simple Machines?

Simple machines make our work easier. They can magnify the force we use, they may change the direction of the force, and they can make our force more effective. A simple machine is made of only one simple part.

The Simple Machines in the Pictures

  • Wheel and axle — the wheel of a bicycle or a cart, which makes a load easy to move.
  • Lever — a rod like a crowbar, which helps to lift a heavy object.
  • Pulley — a machine with a rope and a wheel, which helps to lift a load up. A pulley is used to raise a flag.
  • Screw — which has a grooved thread and joins things firmly.
  • Wedge — a machine with a sharp edge, which cuts or splits things. The knife, scissors and axe work on the principle of the wedge, because one edge of them is sharp and the other edge is thick.

Uses of a Wheelbarrow

With a wheelbarrow (a trolley with one wheel) we can carry heavy things easily. It is used for carrying soil, plants and tools in the garden and bricks and sand at a building site. Because of its one wheel and two handles, even a heavy load can be moved with little force.

Key Points

  • Simple machines make work easier and more effective.
  • A pulley is used to raise a flag.
  • Knife, scissors and axe are wedges.
  • A screw joins things firmly.

mcqs.q: Which simple machine is used to raise a flag?
mcqs.why: A pulley is used to raise a flag. It is a machine with a rope and a wheel, which helps to lift a load up.

mcqs.q: A knife, scissors and an axe work on the principle of the:
mcqs.why: All these machines work on the principle of the wedge, because one edge of them is sharp and the other edge is thick.

mcqs.q: Which machine has a grooved thread and joins things firmly?
mcqs.why: A screw has a grooved thread and joins things firmly. All the parts of a bicycle are joined with screws.

mcqs.q: A crowbar, which helps to lift a heavy object, is a:
mcqs.why: A lever is a rod like a crowbar, which helps to lift a heavy object with less force.

mcqs.q: The wheel of a bicycle or a cart is an example of:
mcqs.why: Wheel and axle — the wheel of a bicycle or a cart makes a load easy to move.

mcqs.q: A wheelbarrow is used to:
options: Carry heavy things easily from one place to another
mcqs.why: With a wheelbarrow we can carry heavy things easily. It is used for carrying soil, plants and tools in the garden and bricks and sand at a building site.

mcqs.q: Which statement about simple machines is correct?
options: Simple machines can make your force more effective
Simple machines never change direction of force
mcqs.why: Simple machines magnify the force you use, may change the direction of the force, and can make your force more effective.

mcqs.q: Why can a heavy load be moved with little force in a wheelbarrow?
options: Because of its one wheel and two handles
Because it is made of plastic
mcqs.why: Because of its one wheel and two handles, even a heavy load can be moved with little force in a wheelbarrow.

mcqs.q: Three machines that help us to cut an object into two pieces are:
mcqs.why: Three machines that help us in cutting are the knife, the scissors and the axe (or saw). All work as wedges.

mcqs.q: A pulley helps us to:
mcqs.why: A pulley is a machine with a rope and a wheel, which helps to lift a load up, such as raising a flag.

lessons.title: Compound Machines and Machines Around Us
lessons.notes_html:
Simple and Compound Machines

Similarity: both simple and compound machines make our work easier and both need force to work. Difference: a simple machine is made of only one simple part, such as the lever, pulley and wedge, while a compound machine is made by joining two or more simple machines, such as the bicycle and the wheelbarrow.

Simple Machines in a Bicycle

  • Wheel and axle — both wheels help the bicycle to move easily.
  • Lever — the handle and brake levers help to change the direction and to stop the bicycle; the pedals also work like levers.
  • Screw — all the parts of the bicycle are joined firmly with screws.

Machines at Home and School

At home: scissors, knife, rolling pin, the pulley of a well or bucket, needle and axe. At school: the flag pulley, scissors, paper-cutting machine and the hinges of doors (lever).

Project: A Load-Carrying Cart

Fix four small wheels under a strong wooden board with screws, so the board becomes a trolley. Tie a handle of strong string at the front to pull the cart. Place the load in the middle and tie it with the string. Because of the wheels, even a heavy load of 70 kg moves easily with little force, because the wheels reduce friction.

Key Points

  • A compound machine joins two or more simple machines.
  • A bicycle has wheel and axle, levers and screws.
  • Wheels reduce friction, so heavy loads move easily.

mcqs.q: A compound machine is made by joining:
mcqs.why: A compound machine is made by joining two or more simple machines, such as the bicycle and the wheelbarrow.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a compound machine?
mcqs.why: The bicycle is a compound machine because it joins wheel and axle, levers and screws together.

mcqs.q: How are simple and compound machines similar?
options: Both make our work easier and both need force to work
Both are used only at home
mcqs.why: Both machines make our work easier and both need force to work. This is their similarity.

mcqs.q: Which simple machines are used in a bicycle?
options: Wheel and axle, lever and screw
mcqs.why: A bicycle has three main simple machines: wheel and axle, lever (handle, brakes, pedals) and screw (joining all parts).

mcqs.q: The pedals and brake levers of a bicycle work like a:
mcqs.why: The handle and brake levers help to change direction and stop the bicycle, and the pedals also work like levers.

mcqs.q: Which machine at school works as a lever?
mcqs.why: Machines found at school include the flag pulley, scissors, paper-cutting machine and the hinges of doors, which work as a lever.

mcqs.q: In the cart project, why does a heavy load of 70 kg move easily?
mcqs.why: Because of the wheels, even a heavy load of 70 kg will move easily with little force, because the wheels reduce friction.

mcqs.q: A rolling pin at home is listed among machines that work as a:
mcqs.why: Machines found at home include scissors, knife, rolling pin, the pulley of a well or bucket, needle and axe.

mcqs.q: A wheelbarrow is an example of a:
mcqs.why: A wheelbarrow is counted among compound machines because it joins simple machines like the wheel and axle and levers (handles).

mcqs.q: In the cart design, the load should be placed:
options: In the middle of the board and tied with string
mcqs.why: Place the load in the middle of the board and tie it with the string so that it does not move while the cart is pulled.

lessons.title: How Sound is Produced
lessons.notes_html:
Sound and Vibrations

Sound is produced by vibrations. Vibrations mean to shake or to move. When a drum is beaten, its skin vibrates and sound comes out. Plucking the string of a sitar also makes the string vibrate and produce sound.

Words of This Unit

  • Medium — something through which sound passes.
  • Noise — unwanted sound.
  • Decibel — the measurement unit of sound.
  • Pitch — the highness or the lowness of a voice.

Key Points

  • Sound is produced when an object vibrates.
  • Decibel is the unit used to measure sound.
  • Pitch is the highness or lowness of a voice.

mcqs.q: Sound is produced when an object:
mcqs.why: Sound is produced when an object vibrates. When a drum is beaten, its skin vibrates and sound comes out.

mcqs.q: The measurement unit of sound is:
mcqs.why: Decibel is the measurement unit of sound, as matched in the columns of this unit.

mcqs.q: Pitch means:
options: The highness or the lowness of a voice
mcqs.why: Pitch is the highness or the lowness of a voice. A thin voice has a high pitch and a heavy voice has a low pitch.

mcqs.q: A medium is:
mcqs.why: A medium is something through which sound passes, such as air, water or a solid like wood or string.

mcqs.q: Noise is:
mcqs.why: Noise is unwanted sound. When a sound is very loud, unwanted and troubling, we experience it as noise.

mcqs.q: When the string of a sitar is plucked, sound is produced because the string:
mcqs.why: Plucking the string of a sitar makes the string vibrate, and this vibration produces sound.

mcqs.q: Vibrations mean:
mcqs.why: Vibrations mean to shake or to move. Sound is produced by vibrations of objects.

mcqs.q: When a drum is beaten, which part vibrates to produce sound?
mcqs.why: When a drum is beaten, its skin vibrates and sound comes out. Without vibration there would be no sound.

mcqs.q: Which of these will produce sound?
mcqs.why: Only a vibrating object produces sound. A vibrating guitar string shakes and makes sound, like the sitar string.

mcqs.q: If an object stops vibrating, the sound it makes will:
mcqs.why: Sound is produced by vibrations, so when the vibration stops, the sound also stops.

lessons.title: How Sound Travels
lessons.notes_html:
Sound Needs a Medium

Sound travels through three mediums: gas (air), liquid (water) and solids (wood, iron, etc.). Sound travels fastest in solids, then in liquids, and slowest in air.

Sound Cannot Travel in a Vacuum

Sound needs some medium to travel, because it moves forward by the vibration of particles. In a vacuum there are no particles or air, so sound cannot travel in a vacuum and there is complete silence there.

Project: A String Telephone

Make a small hole in the bottom of each of two polystyrene cups, pass one end of a copper string through it and tie it with a paper clip; prepare the second cup in the same way. Keeping the string straight and tight, one friend puts a cup to his ear and the other speaks into his cup. The sound reaches from one cup to the other by the vibration of the string. This shows that sound can travel through a solid medium (the string).

Key Points

  • Sound travels through solids, liquids and gases.
  • Sound travels fastest in solids and slowest in air.
  • Sound cannot travel in a vacuum.

mcqs.q: Sound travels through which mediums?
mcqs.why: Sound travels through three mediums: gas (air), liquid (water) and solids (wood, iron, etc.).

mcqs.q: Sound travels fastest in:
mcqs.why: Sound travels fastest in solids, then in liquids and slowest in air. In a vacuum it cannot travel at all.

mcqs.q: Sound travels slowest in:
mcqs.why: Sound travels slowest in air (gas), faster in liquids and fastest in solids like wood and iron.

mcqs.q: Why can sound not travel in a vacuum?
options: Because it is too dark there
Because there are no particles or air in a vacuum
mcqs.why: Sound moves forward by the vibration of particles. In a vacuum there are no particles or air, so sound cannot travel there.

mcqs.q: In a vacuum, there is:
mcqs.why: Sound cannot travel in a vacuum, so there is complete silence there.

mcqs.q: In the string telephone, sound travels from one cup to the other through:
options: The vibration of the string (a solid)
mcqs.why: The sound reaches from one cup to the other by the vibration of the string, which shows sound can travel through a solid medium.

mcqs.q: For the string telephone to work well, the string should be kept:
mcqs.why: Keeping the string straight and tight, one friend speaks into a cup and the other hears through the cup at his ear.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a liquid medium for sound?
mcqs.why: Water is a liquid medium. Wood and iron are solids, and air is a gas; sound travels through all three kinds.

mcqs.q: Sound moves forward by:
mcqs.why: Sound needs a medium because it moves forward by the vibration of particles of the medium.

mcqs.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Sound can travel without any medium
Sound travels faster in air than in iron
Sound cannot travel in a vacuum
mcqs.why: Sound cannot travel in a vacuum because there are no particles there. It travels fastest in solids like iron.

lessons.title: Noise and Its Effects
lessons.notes_html:
What is Noise?

When a sound is very loud, unwanted and troubling, we experience it as noise. For example, the horns of vehicles, the noise of a bazaar and the sound of machines are noise, which troubles our ears.

Sources of Noise

The main sources of noise are: the horns and engines of vehicles, the machines of factories, loud music and loudspeakers, the sound of aeroplanes, and the noise of bazaars and fairs.

Handling Noise

Asma lives near an airport where there is noise all day and night. She should keep the doors and windows of her house closed and hang thick curtains on the windows, because they reduce the sound. While studying, she can use cotton or earplugs in her ears, and planting trees around the house will also reduce the noise.

Protect Your Ears

Listening to music at a high volume with earphones for a long time can damage the ears and the hearing ability can become weak. Headache, dizziness and not being able to concentrate can also occur, so the volume should always be kept low.

Campaign Against Noise Pollution

Put posters and banners about noise pollution in the school and tell the students in the morning assembly that loud sound is harmful for the ears and health. Advise people to blow horns less, listen to music at a low volume and keep silence near hospitals and schools.

Key Points

  • Noise is loud, unwanted and troubling sound.
  • Thick curtains, closed windows and trees reduce noise.
  • High-volume earphone music can damage hearing.
  • Keep silence near hospitals and schools.

mcqs.q: We experience a sound as noise when it is:
mcqs.why: When a sound is very loud, unwanted and troubling, we experience it as noise, like the horns of vehicles.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a source of noise?
options: The horns and engines of vehicles
mcqs.why: The main sources of noise are the horns and engines of vehicles, machines of factories, loud music and loudspeakers, aeroplanes and bazaars.

mcqs.q: Asma lives near an airport. What will reduce the noise in her house?
options: Keeping doors and windows closed and hanging thick curtains
mcqs.why: She should keep the doors and windows closed and hang thick curtains, because they reduce the sound coming inside.

mcqs.q: While studying in noise, Asma can use:
options: Cotton or earplugs in her ears
mcqs.why: While studying, she can use cotton or earplugs in her ears to avoid the noise, and trees around the house also reduce noise.

mcqs.q: Listening to music at high volume with earphones for a long time can:
options: Damage the ears and weaken hearing ability
mcqs.why: It can damage the ears and the hearing ability can become weak. Headache, dizziness and poor concentration can also occur.

mcqs.q: To protect the ears, the volume of music should be kept:
mcqs.why: The volume should always be kept low, because high volume for long periods damages the ears.

mcqs.q: Planting trees around a house helps against noise because trees:
mcqs.why: Planting trees around the house will also reduce the noise coming from outside, like the noise near an airport.

mcqs.q: In a noise pollution campaign, people should be advised to:
options: Blow horns less and keep silence near hospitals and schools
mcqs.why: People should be advised to blow horns less, listen to music at a low volume and keep silence near hospitals and schools.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of noise?
mcqs.why: The horns of vehicles, the noise of a bazaar and the sound of machines are noise, which troubles our ears.

mcqs.q: Loud sound is harmful for:
mcqs.why: In the morning assembly students are told that loud sound is harmful for the ears and health. That is why noise pollution should be reduced.

lessons.title: Conductors and Insulators
lessons.notes_html:
Conductors

Conductors are those materials through which electricity passes easily: (1) copper, (2) iron, (3) aluminium, (4) steel and (5) silver.

Insulators

Insulators are those materials through which electricity does not pass: (1) plastic, (2) rubber, (3) wood, (4) glass and (5) paper. Insulators are used for safety from electricity and for covering wires.

Why Wires are Covered

Wires are made of copper because electricity passes easily through it, and a layer of plastic or rubber is put over them so that we stay safe from the current. Plastic wires are not used in electrical appliances at home; the wires are metal, covered with plastic.

Key Points

  • Conductors: copper, iron, aluminium, steel, silver.
  • Insulators: plastic, rubber, wood, glass, paper.
  • Wires are copper inside and plastic or rubber outside.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a conductor of electricity?
mcqs.why: Conductors are materials through which electricity passes easily: copper, iron, aluminium, steel and silver.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an insulator?
mcqs.why: Insulators are materials through which electricity does not pass: plastic, rubber, wood, glass and paper.

mcqs.q: Wires are made of copper and covered with plastic because:
options: Electricity passes easily through copper and plastic keeps us safe
mcqs.why: Wires are made of copper because current passes easily through it, and a layer of plastic or rubber over them keeps us safe.

mcqs.q: Which material cannot be used to complete an electric circuit?
mcqs.why: Wood is an insulator, so it cannot be used to complete an electric circuit. Copper wire, iron nail and graphite are conductors.

mcqs.q: How many conductors are listed in this unit?
options: Five: copper, iron, aluminium, steel, silver
mcqs.why: Five conductors are listed: (1) copper, (2) iron, (3) aluminium, (4) steel and (5) silver.

mcqs.q: Insulators are used for:
options: Safety from electricity and for covering wires
mcqs.why: Insulators such as plastic, rubber and wood are used for safety from electricity and for covering wires.

mcqs.q: Which statement is false?
options: Plastic wires are used in electrical appliances at home
mcqs.why: The statement 'Plastic wires are used in electrical appliances at home' is false. The wires are metal conductors covered with plastic.

mcqs.q: Which of these groups contains only insulators?
mcqs.why: Plastic, rubber and wood are all insulators. Copper, iron, steel, aluminium and silver are conductors.

mcqs.q: Steel is a:
mcqs.why: Steel is listed among the conductors: copper, iron, aluminium, steel and silver all let electricity pass easily.

mcqs.q: Paper is an example of a:
mcqs.why: Paper is one of the five insulators listed in this unit: plastic, rubber, wood, glass and paper.

lessons.title: Electric Circuits
lessons.notes_html:
Making a Simple Circuit

Take a wire from one end of the cell and join it to the switch. Join a wire from the other end of the switch to the bulb, and join a wire from the other end of the bulb back to the other end of the cell. In this way a closed round path is made.

Open and Closed Circuits
