  • In an open circuit the path of electricity is broken, so current does not flow and the bulb does not light up.
  • In a closed circuit the path is complete and joined, so current flows and the bulb lights up.
  • The circuit is closed when the switch is on. Turning the switch off opens the circuit and the bulb goes out.

Current is the flow of electric charges through the circuit.

Key Points

  • A circuit is a closed round path of cell, switch and bulb.
  • Switch on means the circuit is closed and the bulb glows.
  • Switch off means the circuit is open and the bulb goes out.

mcqs.q: A circuit is closed when the switch is:
mcqs.why: The circuit is closed when the switch is on. This statement is true: current then flows and the bulb lights up.

mcqs.q: In an open circuit:
options: The path of electricity is broken, so current does not flow
mcqs.why: In an open circuit the path of electricity is broken, so current does not flow and the bulb does not light up.

mcqs.q: In a closed circuit:
options: The path is complete, so current flows and the bulb lights up
mcqs.why: In a closed circuit the path is complete and joined, so current flows and the bulb lights up.

mcqs.q: To make a circuit, the cell, switch and bulb are joined by:
options: Wires, in a closed round path
mcqs.why: Wires join the cell to the switch, the switch to the bulb, and the bulb back to the cell, making a closed round path.

mcqs.q: What happens when the switch is turned off?
options: The circuit opens and the bulb goes out
mcqs.why: Turning the switch off will open the circuit and the bulb will go out, because the path of electricity is broken.

mcqs.q: Current is:
mcqs.why: Current is the movement (flow) of electric charges through the circuit. The book states it as the movement of charges.

mcqs.q: Which thing is needed to control the flow of current in the circuit?
mcqs.why: The switch controls the circuit: turning it on closes the circuit and turning it off opens the circuit.

mcqs.q: If one wire is removed from the circuit, the bulb will:
options: Not light up, because the circuit is open
mcqs.why: Removing a wire breaks the round path, making an open circuit, so current does not flow and the bulb does not light up.

mcqs.q: The source of electricity in the simple circuit is the:
mcqs.why: The cell (battery) is the source of electricity in the simple circuit of cell, switch and bulb.

mcqs.q: Which statement is correct?
options: An open circuit makes the bulb glow
A closed circuit has a broken path
A closed circuit lets current flow and the bulb lights up
A switch is not part of a circuit
mcqs.why: In a closed circuit the path is complete and joined, so current flows and the bulb lights up. An open circuit has the broken path.

lessons.title: Magnets and Their Uses
lessons.notes_html:
Magnetic and Non-Magnetic Materials

Magnetic materials are those which a magnet attracts towards itself, such as iron, steel and nickel. Non-magnetic materials are those which a magnet does not attract, such as wood, plastic, copper and paper. Steel is a magnetic material.

Poles of a Magnet

Like poles repel each other, and unlike poles attract. The poles of a freely suspended magnet point towards the North and South of the Earth.

Permanent and Temporary Magnets

A permanent magnet always keeps its magnetic effect and it cannot be finished, like a bar magnet. A temporary magnet becomes a magnet only when electricity passes through it, and when the electricity is stopped, its effect ends, like an electromagnet. A steel rod can be temporarily magnetised by passing electric current around it.

Uses of Magnets

  • In a compass, the magnetic needle shows the direction, with which travellers and pilots find their way.
  • A magnet is used to pick up and separate pins, nails and other iron things, such as separating iron from garbage.
  • Magnets are used in the doors and fasteners of fridges and bags so that they stay tightly closed. Magnets are also used in motors and speakers.

Project: Finding the Poles

Take a marked magnet whose poles are known. Bring one end of the unmarked magnet near the north pole of the known magnet; if that end is pushed away (repelled), it is also the north pole, and if it is attracted, it is the south pole.

Key Points

  • A magnet attracts iron, steel and nickel.
  • Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.
  • A suspended magnet points North and South.
  • Magnets are used in compasses, fridge doors, motors and speakers.

mcqs.q: Which thing is attracted towards a magnet?
mcqs.why: An iron kettle is attracted towards a magnet, because iron is a magnetic material. Copper and wood are non-magnetic.

mcqs.q: Like poles of two magnets:
mcqs.why: Like poles repel each other. This is also used to find the poles of an unmarked magnet in the project.

mcqs.q: The poles of a suspended magnet point towards:
options: North and South of the Earth
mcqs.why: The poles of a suspended magnet point towards the North and South of the Earth respectively. That is how a compass works.

mcqs.q: A steel rod can be temporarily magnetised by:
mcqs.why: A steel rod can be temporarily magnetised by passing electric current around it, like an electromagnet.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a non-magnetic material?
mcqs.why: Non-magnetic materials are those which a magnet does not attract, such as wood, plastic, copper and paper.

mcqs.q: The statement 'Steel is a non-magnetic material' is:
mcqs.why: This statement is false. Steel is a magnetic material, attracted by magnets, along with iron and nickel.

mcqs.q: A permanent magnet is one which:
options: Always keeps its magnetic effect, like a bar magnet
Loses its effect in one day
mcqs.why: A permanent magnet always keeps its magnetic effect and it cannot be finished, like a bar magnet.

mcqs.q: A temporary magnet becomes a magnet only when:
mcqs.why: A temporary magnet becomes a magnet only when electricity passes through it, and when the electricity is stopped, its effect ends.

mcqs.q: Which is a use of magnets?
options: In a compass, the needle shows the direction
mcqs.why: In a compass, the magnetic needle shows the direction, with which travellers and pilots find their way.

mcqs.q: To find the pole of an unmarked magnet, if its end is repelled by the known north pole, that end is the:
mcqs.why: Like poles repel each other, so if the end is pushed away by the known north pole, it is also the north pole.

lessons.title: The Earth: Axis, Poles and Equator
lessons.notes_html:
The Earth is a Sphere

The Earth is a planet and it is shaped like a sphere — a completely round shape. The statement 'The Earth is not a sphere' is false.

Words of This Unit

  • Axis — the imaginary line on which the Earth rotates. An axis is a line.
  • Poles — the two ends of the Earth, North and South. The Earth has poles.
  • Equator — the imaginary line in the middle of the Earth.
  • Hemispheres — the two halves of the Earth.
  • Orbit — the path of the Earth around the Sun. The elongated circular orbit of the Earth is called an ellipse.
  • Day — the side of the Earth where the light of the Sun falls. Night — the side of the Earth where light does not fall.

The Tilt of the Earth

The Earth is tilted at 23.5° on its axis. This tilt, together with its movements, gives us day, night and the seasons.

Key Points

  • The Earth is a sphere-shaped planet.
  • The axis is an imaginary line.
  • The equator divides the Earth into two hemispheres.
  • The Earth is tilted at 23.5 degrees.

mcqs.q: The Earth is tilted at:
mcqs.why: The Earth is tilted at 23.5 degrees on its axis. This tilt is a cause of the seasons.

mcqs.q: An axis is a:
mcqs.why: An axis is a line — the imaginary line on which the Earth rotates.

mcqs.q: The equator is:
options: A real wire around the Earth
The imaginary line in the middle of the Earth
mcqs.why: The equator is the imaginary line in the middle of the Earth. It divides the Earth into two hemispheres.

mcqs.q: Hemispheres are:
options: The two ends of the Earth
The two halves of the Earth
mcqs.why: Hemispheres are the two halves of the Earth, divided by the equator.

mcqs.q: The poles are:
options: The two ends of the Earth, North and South
The middle line of the Earth
mcqs.why: The poles are the two ends of the Earth, North and South. The statement 'The Earth has no poles' is false.

mcqs.q: The elongated circular orbit of the Earth is called an:
mcqs.why: The elongated circular orbit of the Earth is called an ellipse. The orbit is the path of the Earth around the Sun.

mcqs.q: A sphere is:
mcqs.why: A sphere is a completely round shape. The Earth is shaped like a sphere.

mcqs.q: The side of the Earth where the light of the Sun falls has:
mcqs.why: Day is the side of the Earth where the light of the Sun falls, and night is the side where light does not fall.

mcqs.q: The statement 'The Earth is not a sphere' is:
mcqs.why: This statement is false, because the Earth is a sphere — a completely round planet.

mcqs.q: The Earth is a:
mcqs.why: The Earth is the planet on which we live. It makes two movements: rotation and revolution.

lessons.title: Rotation: Day and Night
lessons.notes_html:
Rotation

Rotation is the spinning of the Earth on its axis. The Earth takes 24 hours to complete one rotation. It is not true that rotation takes one year and 6 hours — that is the time of revolution.

Day and Night

Rotation causes day and night. The part of the Earth that faces the Sun will have day, and the side of the Earth which is away from the Sun has night. The Earth rotates towards the East.

Unscramble and Make a Sentence

TOTIRNOA = ROTATION, SAUSEC = CAUSES, YDA = DAY, NAD = AND, HINTG = NIGHT. The sentence is: ROTATION CAUSES DAY AND NIGHT. It is because of the rotation of the Earth that day and night are formed.

Key Points

  • Rotation is the spinning of the Earth on its axis.
  • One rotation takes 24 hours.
  • Rotation causes day and night.
  • The Earth rotates towards the East.

mcqs.q: How long does the Earth take to complete one rotation?
mcqs.why: The Earth takes 24 hours to complete one rotation on its axis. Rotation causes day and night.

mcqs.q: Rotation of the Earth causes:
mcqs.why: Rotation causes day and night. The unscrambled sentence of this unit is: ROTATION CAUSES DAY AND NIGHT.

mcqs.q: The part of the Earth that faces the Sun will have:
mcqs.why: The part of the Earth that faces the Sun will have day, and the side away from the Sun has night.

mcqs.q: The Earth rotates towards the:
mcqs.why: The rotating direction of the Earth is towards the East. That is why the Sun appears to rise in the east.

mcqs.q: The statement 'The revolution of Earth takes 24 hours' is:
mcqs.why: This statement is false. It is rotation that takes 24 hours; revolution takes 365 days and 6 hours.

mcqs.q: The statement 'The rotation of Earth takes one year and 6 hours' is:
mcqs.why: This statement is false. Rotation takes 24 hours; one year and 6 hours (365 days and 6 hours) is the time of revolution.

mcqs.q: Rotation means:
options: The spinning of the Earth on its axis
mcqs.why: Rotation is the spinning of the Earth on its axis. Moving around the Sun is called revolution.

mcqs.q: The side of the Earth away from the Sun has:
mcqs.why: The side of the Earth which is away from the Sun has night, because the light of the Sun does not fall there.

mcqs.q: How many movements does the Earth make?
mcqs.why: The Earth makes two movements: rotation and revolution. The statement that the Earth has only one movement is false.

mcqs.q: Unscramble TOTIRNOA:

lessons.title: Revolution and Seasons
lessons.notes_html:
Revolution

Revolution is the movement of the Earth around the Sun in its orbit. The Earth completes one revolution around the Sun in 365 days and 6 hours.

Seasons

Due to rotation and revolution, seasons are formed. When one hemisphere of the Earth is tilted towards the Sun, it is summer there: days are longer and nights are shorter. In the part away from the Sun it is winter: days are shorter. We have shorter days in winter and longer days in summer. The four seasons of the year are spring, summer, winter and autumn. On 21st or 22nd March, the day and night are equal in both hemispheres; days and nights are also equal in spring and autumn.

Project: A Hanging Model of the Solar System

Make the large yellow ball the Sun and colour the eight small balls as the eight planets, writing the name of each on it. Make the ring of Saturn from a cardboard circle piece. Tie each ball with strings of different lengths, hanging the Sun in the middle and the planets around it in order: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

Key Points

  • Revolution is the Earth's movement around the Sun.
  • One revolution takes 365 days and 6 hours.
  • Revolution and the tilt cause the seasons.
  • Days are longer in summer and shorter in winter.

mcqs.q: The Earth completes one revolution around the Sun in:
mcqs.why: The Earth completes one revolution around the Sun in 365 days and 6 hours. Rotation takes only 24 hours.

mcqs.q: We have shorter days in:
mcqs.why: We have shorter days in winter, when our hemisphere is tilted away from the Sun.

mcqs.q: We have longer days in:
mcqs.why: We have longer days in summer, when our hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun.

mcqs.q: When one hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, the season there is:
mcqs.why: When one hemisphere of the Earth is tilted towards the Sun, it is summer there. This statement is true.

mcqs.q: On 21st or 22nd March:
options: Day and night are equal in both hemispheres
mcqs.why: On 21st or 22nd March, the day and night are equal in both hemispheres. This statement is true.

mcqs.q: Seasons are formed due to:
options: Rotation and revolution of the Earth
mcqs.why: Due to rotation and revolution, seasons are formed. The tilt of the Earth with revolution gives summer and winter.

mcqs.q: The statement 'Due to revolution, seasons and day and night are formed' is not fully correct because:
options: Revolution forms only day and night
Day and night are formed by rotation, not revolution
Seasons are formed by the Moon
mcqs.why: Day and night are formed by rotation. Revolution, with the tilt, forms the seasons. So the statement mixing both is false.

mcqs.q: In the part of the Earth tilted away from the Sun, there will be:
mcqs.why: In the part tilted towards the Sun there will be summer, and in the part away there will be winter, with shorter days.

mcqs.q: Which planet comes third in order from the Sun in the model?
mcqs.why: The planets in order are: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Earth is third.

mcqs.q: In the solar system model, the large yellow ball is the:
mcqs.why: The large yellow ball is made the Sun, hung in the middle, and the eight small balls are the planets around it.
